prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can give you specific firm names, but first a couple quick questions so I tailor recommendations to your needs:

- Are you in Dallas city proper or a Dallas-area suburb (Oak Cliff, Plano, Garland, Irving, etc.)?  
- Do you have serious injury/death or mainly vehicle/property damage?  
- Do you prefer a large national firm or a smaller Dallas trial boutique?  

While you answer, here’s immediate, practical guidance so you can start contacting lawyers today:

Why you should call a truck-accident specialist
- Truck cases involve federal/state trucking rules, the carrier, driver’s employer, maintenance records, and often complex insurance policies. A lawyer who handles truck cases regularly will know how to get black-box/ELD data, driver logs, maintenance records, and to identify liable parties (owner, carrier, broker, shipper).
- If injuries are significant, you’ll want someone comfortable taking the case to trial (not just settling quickly).

What to ask when you call (3–5 minute checklist)
- Do you handle truck (commercial vehicle) accidents in Dallas? How many truck cases have you tried?  
- Are you board-certified in personal injury trial law (Texas Board of Legal Specialization)?  
- Do you handle cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover)? What is your contingency percentage and who pays expenses?  
- Who exactly will work my case (partner, associate, paralegal)? Will you be my point of contact?  
- Have you recovered verdicts/settlements against large trucking companies or insurers? Can you give examples?  
- How long do you expect investigation to take and what evidence will you obtain (ELD, driver logs, maintenance records, witnesses)?  
- Do you have experience with catastrophic injury / wrongful-death claims (if applicable)?  

Important deadlines
- In Texas you generally have 2 years from the date of a personal-injury crash to file suit (Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code §16.003); wrongful death also generally 2 years. Call a lawyer promptly — evidence (truck logs, surveillance, vehicle parts) disappears fast.

How to prioritize calls
- First call: a Dallas trial firm that specializes in truck/catastrophic-injury cases. They’ll preserve evidence and move quickly.  
- Second: a reputable national firm with a Dallas presence if you want big-resources representation.  
- Third: a local boutique with strong trial experience if you want a smaller, more personal team.

If you want, I’ll compile a short list of Dallas firms (with reasons to call each) based on whether you want big-national or local boutique — tell me your preference and any other details (severity of injuries, whether there were fatalities, whether you know the carrier).
